options.act: Main window: Needs-you row + tile badges; project window: full the board + overview; Boards window: cross-project review mode
options.label: Three shapes: a count in the main window, the room in a project window, the zone in the Boards window
options.then: Give each window its own the board: a count in the main window, the full room in a project window, and review mode in the Boards window.

options.label: The same view in every window

why: The main window is for running things, so the board there is only a count and a doorway. A project window is where you work on one project, so the board there is the whole picture of that project. The Boards window is for working through what needs you, so it opens in review mode. This is how Xcode treats its main window, the Organizer and a torn-off editor.

summary: Switchboard already pops a project out into its own window ("Bring Back" puts it back), reopens those windows at launch, and gives each window its own split panes and sidebar width. The board should look different in each window, because each window is there for a different reason.
title: One board, three shapes, depending on the window
